codes.name: Trust in Local Helpers
codes.definition: People place great trust in neighbors, friends, volunteers, and other known individuals who provide direct help. Rebuilding institutional trust is linked to more open, honest, and responsive communication with communities. Trust is sustained through local civic, service, and volunteer organizations that bring community members together to address shared needs, support one another, and develop local leadership. These organizations may be trusted more than distant or contested public institutions, particularly when public funding or institutional support is perceived as inadequate.

highlights.insight_text: People trust individuals they know—neighbors, friends, volunteers, and local helpers—more than government or other formal leadership. The reflection describes people as “very clearly disappointed in the federal response or even state level response,” while still trusting individual and volunteer action.
